checks: Found no work_summary.md and no Q26 entry in /output/report.json; the only products are out/q26/q26_ratios.{log,json}, scripts/q26_image.py, q26_measure.py and a failed q26_uvdump.py (Xb55 branch crashed with an IndexError, so no uv-plane test exists). The item is therefore not answered on the record.

Re-ran scripts/q26_measure.py and reproduced the table exactly (team/checks/q26_check.py inspects the images). The numbers are not usable. The 8-12" annulus fluxes are NEGATIVE for both 3-2 sets: Xb4f u>6: HCN -25.5, HCO+ -18.1 Jy km/s (R=1.41); Xb4f u>8: -35.6/-55.8 (R=0.64); Xb4d: -37.6/-56.6 (R=0.67). A ratio of two negative numbers is the ratio of the clean-bowl/sidelobe depression, not of emission. The 3-2 ratio is therefore NOT 'positive and measurable' at 8-12", and the table cannot answer whether it falls relative to 2-1 (Xb55 2-1 8-12" is positive, R=0.58+-0.02 at u>6, 0.51+-0.03 at u>8).

The uv-range is not matched. Xb4d (12-m compact) gives IDENTICAL results for uvmin 6 and 8 kl (HCN 10.91/16.96 in 0-4", 0.13/0.17 in 4-8"), i.e. it has no baselines below ~8 kl (12-m shortest ~15 m ~ 13 kl at 265 GHz); at a 10" beam it contains essentially no flux beyond the central annulus (total spectrum sum is negative, about -1 Jy, the signature of a pure bowl). It cannot be 'matched' to Xb55/Xb4f at 6 kl. Xb4f (7-m, shortest ~9 m ~ 8 kl at 265 GHz) changes drastically between u>6 and u>8 (4-8" HCN 26.9 -> 11.1, HCO+ 51.8 -> 16.7 Jy km/s, R 0.52 -> 0.67), while Xb55 2-1 moves only 5-20%. So the u>6 kl set is dominated by the 7-m shortest-baseline sampling and the u>8 set is not matched either: 2-1 (Xb55, 7-m shortest ~9 m = 5 kl at 177 GHz) is sampled down to 5 kl while 3-2 is not below 8 kl. A truly common range in lambda has to start where both have coverage with similar density (u>~9-10 kl) and then 10" structure is mostly filtered; the question has to be re-posed as a uv-plane test, not an annulus-flux test.

Cleaning did not work, so Jy/beam scaling is suspect. q26_image.log: 'No regions found by automasking' in nearly all channels and 'Restoring with an empty model image. Only residuals will be processed' (many channels, all 3-2 sets I inspected). With an empty model the 'image' is the dirty/residual map in dirty-beam units, but q26_measure divides by the area of the 10" restoring beam (omp). For a tapered natural-weight dirty beam that is not a 10" Gaussian, with strong negative sidelobes after the u>uvmin cut, the integrated flux is biased by an unknown factor, and the error bars (std of 'off-line' channels, 0.2-0.8 Jy km/s, R errors 1%) ignore this entirely. Flux per channel is also integrated only where the PSF is non-blank (Xb4f 85, Xb4d 69 of 100 channels with data; the Xb4d window is not even fully covered); the line window |v-2780|<350 km/s needs to be confirmed to lie inside the covered channels, and off-line noise channels (|dv|>600) are only ~400 km/s on each side, with possible contamination (H13CN/SO/CH3OH wings near HCN/HCO+ at 3-2).

The ratios of 0-4" annulus (R=0.60-0.65 for 2-1 and 3-2 at both u cuts) are the only stable values, but at 10" resolution this annulus contains N, S and the bridge and tells us nothing new beyond Q22, and it shows no 2-1 -> 3-2 fall (0.65/0.65, 0.64 within 1-2%). Systematic differences between u>6 and u>8 (up to 10-30%) are 5-30x the quoted statistical errors, so the quoted +-0.005-0.02 errors are not credible. No null test (HCN/HCO+ ratio of an off-line channel range, or a simulated source observed with the same uv sampling) was run.

Conclusion on convention/calibration: PB>0.5 with 84-100% area fraction is fine and the annuli follow Q11, but a convincing answer needs a measurement that survives the transfer function; at present the worker's data say that the 8-12" 3-2 emission cannot be recovered with a u>~8 kl cut and 10" beam, which is itself a useful, quantifiable limit that was not derived.
